text:
One way or another, Portugal’s No 7 shirt has caused quite the commotion in recent weeks and months, if not years. Perhaps it was inevitable, then, that the first win of the post-Cristiano Ronaldo era would come courtesy of the player wearing the updated jersey, one with a cross through the number to preserve Ronaldo’s eternal legacy, as the Portuguese football federation put it. A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards.
Turn a new page and all that. This was a welcome victory for Jorge Jesus, for whom a 4-1 home defeat to Denmark a few days ago was a harrowing juncture, and there were plenty of positive takeaways for Wales, too. David Brooks cancelled out Bruno Fernandes’s opener from the edge of the box and then seized the lead through Sorba Thomas, who applied the finishing touch to a purring team move. But Neto, who picked up two bookings in one minute and 59 seconds, the second for a foul on Brennan Johnson, equalised before half-time. Craig Bellamy’s side were fun and, at times, freewheeling but Forbs had the final say with a neat run and finish.
Bellamy stressed the importance of locking down Vitinha and João Neves, two of his favourite players who have won successive Champions League titles, and Wales did not allow the Paris Saint-Germain pair to have things all their own way. Vitinha, always scanning and ready to take the ball from his teammates, naturally topped the pass-o-meter, completing all 76 passes he made in an absorbing first half. It was a loose Renato Veiga pass, meant for Vitinha, on the verge of the half-time interval that supplied the all-action Harry Wilson with a speculative opportunity from halfway. Wilson intercepted the ball and, after taking a touch to roll the ball into the opposition half, the Leeds midfielder sent a marvellous left-footed lobbed effort towards goal, his 45-yard shot skimming the roof of Diogo Costa’s goal much to the relief of the Portugal goalkeeper.
Portugal may have levelled a few moments earlier, Neto easily beating Jay Dasilva in the six-yard box to prod in Francisco Trincão’s brilliant cross, but Wilson’s attempt at the audacious was another gentle reminder of Portugal’s precarious state. This was a ludicrously open game and, after leaking four goals at home for the first time in an international game in last weekend’s humiliating 4-1 defeat to Denmark in Braga, Portugal were again susceptible defensively. Before Thomas capped a scintillating team move to seize the lead on 40 minutes, Wilson twice went close, Diogo Dalot making a desperate block for the first before the second from another electric team move.
Portugal made four changes from Saturday’s stinging defeat, with the Bournemouth centre-back António Silva replacing the suspended Rúben Dias and Neves, shirt tucked into his shorts, joining Vitinha at the base of midfield. Trincão was lively down the left wing and the marauding João Cancelo a constant threat, popping up all over the pitch. When Fernandes picked his spot on 11 minutes, sending an unerring strike into the top corner, Portugal appeared in the groove.
But Wales responded two minutes later when Brooks, who scored courtesy of a superb dinked finish in defeat by Norway, dug out another clever finish. Wilson saw a shot repelled by Costa at the Porto goalkeeper’s near post and, when the ball squirted free, Rubin Colwill had the presence of mind to calmly square for Brooks, who squeezed a left-foot shot into the far corner. Colwill, a fan favourite here for Cardiff, thoroughly enjoyed his first Wales start. Brooks, another one of the six players promoted to Bellamy’s starting XI, neatly dovetailed with the busy Wilson.
This was an entertaining occasion for which it was worth braving the winter conditions. Neto wellied a shot against the base of a post after nipping past Ben Davies and Fernandes later released Forbs after a magnificent take to control the ball midway inside his own half.
Colwill impressed in a deep midfield role alongside Josh Sheehan of Bolton, whose former clubmate Aaron Collins, now of MK Dons, arrived from the bench midway through the second half for his debut. Portugal, meanwhile, introduced João Félix and the Club Brugge winger Forbs. Ben Cabango, who replaced Joe Rodon as a precaution at half-time, went close to scoring with a header.
Wales could not regain the lead and instead trailed, though the weary look on Costa’s face as he pawed Cabango’s header away from goal for a corner said it all. The moment Forbs surged on to a loose Cabango header and then at Davies before applying a low left-foot finish provided light relief on another uncomfortable night for Jesus and his Portugal players. For Wales, a challenging Nations League campaign, ended as it began, with a heartening defeat to Portugal.
digest_he:
משחק רב שערים ודרמטי הסתיים בניצחונם של פורטוגל על וויילס במסגרת ליגת האומות, במשחק הראשון של הנבחרת בעידן שאחרי כריסטיאנו רונאלדו. את שער הניצחון כבש המחליף קרלוס פורבס בדקות הסיום, והעניק לנבחרתו של ז'ורז' ז'זוש שלוש נקודות יקרות לאחר משחק פתוח במיוחד.

המשחק כלל תהפוכות רבות כאשר וויילס הפגינה יכולת מרשימה, מחקה פיגור מוקדם ואף עלתה ליתרון זמני בזכות שערים של דיוויד ברוקס וסורבה תומאס, זאת לצד שער יתרון מוקדם של ברונו פרננדש לזכות פורטוגל. למרות הרחקתו של פדרו נטו בגין צהוב כפול, פורטוגל הצליחה להתאושש מהתבוסה שנחלה לאחרונה מול דנמרק ולסיים את קמפיין ליגת האומות בטעם טוב בפסגת הבית.
